pr_title: drivers/entropy: stm32: RNG  configuration on some MCUs
pr_body:
for the entropy/ RNG of some stm32 mcus (like stm32L5x and stm32U5 and stm32H723) when the RNG peripheral has a 
Health Test Control and COND the sequence to
Two properties are defined by the RNG node : 
```
			health-test-magic = <0x17590abc>;
 			health-test-config = <0x9aae>;
```
According to the ref man, the sequence for writing the RNG_HTCR requires to LL_RNG_EnableCondReset before and LL_RNG_DisableCondReset after writing the RNG_HTCR.
According to the ref Man : "When CONDRST is set to 0 by software its value goes to 0 when the reset process is done.
It takes about 2 AHB clock cycles + 2 RNG clock cycles."
This PR adds a loop to wait for the bit to be read as 0.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/45866

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu <francois.ramu@st.com>
pr_comments:
tested with  west build -p auto -b xxx tests/drivers/entropy/api/ 
on  nucleo_u575zi_q and nucleo_l552ze_q

When CONDRST is set, RNG is re-initialized, which adds a latency before entropy to be available. On single core MCUs, `configure_rng()` is done only at entropy driver initialization so this is fine. However, on multi-core MCUs such as STM32H747, `configure_rng()` is invoked for every new entropy generation process and it might be worth checking if RNG_HTCR is already set to the desired value to avoid useless RNG re-initialization.
Note that currently no STM32 MCUs supporting CONDRST are multi-core, but that might change in the future, leading to performance issues.

New version of the driver with the introduction of the `nist-config` property

All the sequence is now under`  #ifdef STM32_CONDRST_SUPPORT `

> > > > On multi-core MCUs such as STM32H747, configure_rng() is invoked for every new entropy generation process and it might be worth checking if RNG_HTCR is already set to the desired value to avoid useless RNG re-initialization.
> > > 
> > > 
> > > In this case, the configure_rng() is done by the acquire_rng(), and could be :
> > > ```
> > > static void acquire_rng(void)
> > > {
> > > #if defined(CONFIG_SOC_SERIES_STM32WBX) || defined(CONFIG_STM32H7_DUAL_CORE)
> > > 	/* Lock the RNG to prevent concurrent access */
> > > 	z_stm32_hsem_lock(CFG_HW_RNG_SEMID, HSEM_LOCK_WAIT_FOREVER);
> > > 	/* RNG configuration could have been changed by the other core */
> > > 	if (LL_RNG_GetHealthConfig(rng) != DT_INST_PROP(0, health_test_config)) {
> > > 		configure_rng();
> > > 	}
> > > #endif /* CONFIG_SOC_SERIES_STM32WBX || CONFIG_STM32H7_DUAL_CORE */
> > > }
> > > ```
> > 
> > 
> > This is not possible because `configure_rng()` does not only write RNG_HTCR and perform NIST-related configuration, it also enables the RNG and RNG IRQ, which could have been disabled by the other core. For example on STM32WB55, the M0 core disables the RNG after use.
> > This also assumes the other core won't change NIST-related configuration (in RNG_CR) without also modifying RNG_HTCR, but I guess in any real world scenario all cores in a MCU will use the exact same "NIST configuration", so that may not be actually an issue
> 
> @taltenbach so is it fine from this perspective ?

It is not in the sense the RNG is reconfigured even if the current configuration was already the proper one. A simple check in `configure_rng()` of the current `RNG_CR` and `RNG_HTCR` values would be sufficient to avoid that. But, as I said, since at present all STM32 MCUs supporting CONDRST are single-core, meaning that `configure_rng()` is only called once at startup, so that is not a real issue at the moment, but might be in the future.

Put the sequence to write the RNG_HTCR  in the configure_rng() as exposed above
Tested with a `health-test-magic = <0x00009aae>; `property in the overlay of the stm32u575 nucleo board.

Perfect, thank you! Just one last point: don't you think it should be a good idea to put the recommended value for `nist-config` in the device trees of the MCUs that support this feature, in the same way this was done for `health-test-config`?

> 
Ok,
 moving the properties `<nist-config>` and `<health-test-magic>` to the stm32 device dtsi
Adding rng node to stm32u575 and stm32h723 nucleo  Boards

Then the overlay is no more useful in the tests/drivers/entropy/api

The register magic number ` health-test-magic = <0x17590abc> `   is given by the RM of the stm32h7a3/b3 and the stm32l5x 
"_When writing this register magic number 0x17590ABC must be written immediately before the indicated value_"

There is no register magic number given for the stm32u5x.

issue_context.title: drivers/entropy: stm32: non-compliant RNG configuration on some MCUs
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
On some STM32 MCUs, such as the STM32H723 or STM32L5, the RNG peripheral must be configured according to specific values provided in the reference manual to obtain best latency and to be compliant with NIST. This includes:
* Writing appropriate values to CONFIG1, CONFIG2 and CONFIG3 fields in RNG_CR register.
* Writing a proper value in RNG_HTCR register. 

However, it seems that the RNG driver:
* Does not write CONFIGx fields, although their reset value does not correspond to the recommended configuration.
* Does not properly follow the process specified in the reference manual to write to RNG_HTCR. Indeed, CONDRST is not set before writing to RNG_HTCR, even though the [RM0468](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0468-stm32h723733-stm32h725735-and-stm32h730-value-line-advanced-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) states (p. 1440):
> Writing in RNG_HTCR is taken into account only if CONDRST bit is set, and CONFIGLOCK bit is cleared in RNG_CR. Writing to this register is ignored if CONFIGLOCK=1.

**To Reproduce**
N/A

**Expected behavior**
The STM32 RNG peripheral should be properly configured. 

**Impact**
RNG configuration is not compliant with NIST and entropy generation latency might not be ideal. 

**Environment**
 Commit e9d3791

**Additional context**
Note that I unfortunately have no STM32 MCU with a RNG peripheral having such configuration fields at my disposal, so this issue is only based on my understanding of the reference manual and the driver implementation. In case the issue turns out to be real, I am willing to create a PR but I won't be able to test the fix on real hardware.
comments:
In the configure_rng(), during the Init sequence, health_test_config and  health_test_magic are set by the `LL_RNG_SetHealthConfig`, once values are defined in the DTS rng node with 
```
			health-test-magic = <0x17590abc>;
			health-test-config = <0xaa74>;
```
However missing before and after LL_RNG_SetHealthConfig : 
	`LL_RNG_EnableCondReset(rng);`
and 
	`LL_RNG_DisableCondReset(rng);`

Precisely! I expect to be able to lay hands next week on a B-U85I-IOT01 board that includes an RNG peripheral with RNG_HTCR register and CONFIGx fields. Therefore, if that's alright with you I can fix the issue next week. Otherwise, if you prefer, I should be able to do the PR earlier but in that case it would be preferable that someone ensures that the entropy driver is still working properly on real hardware

That's the purpose of the https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/45994
As a first step the result is correct. 
There is still another change to apply to follow the sequence of the refMan:
"_CONDRST: Conditioning soft reset : This bit must be set to 1 in the same access that set any configuration bits [29:4]. In other
words, when CONDRST bit is set to 1 correct configuration in bits [29:4] must also be written._"
That means to write the configuration A into the RNG_CR bits  in the configure_rng() function. (There is no LL function for that )

In order to apply the RNG configuration for the NIST certification, the conditions are about the rng_clock source, the RNG_CR register to write and loop , then immediately writing the RNG_HTCR magic nb then immediately writing the RNG_HTCR config nb. 
Because the RNG NIST config can depend on the mcu, a suggestion would be to introduce a new property in the RNG DTS, named `nist-config`
Then for stm32 mcu with this  `nist-config` the sequence is applied in the driver _configure_rng_ : based on the stm32 hal driver function _HAL_RNGEx_SetConfig()_
